[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Across related delivery and tidy tasks, failures occurred when actions were attempted without satisfying their preconditions. Pick-up actions require the target object to be present, nearby, and within reach; attempting pick-up from a distance fails, so navigate to or verify the object's location first. Place actions require the robot to already be holding the target object; if it is not held, complete a pick-up first. Movement actions require a clear path; obstacles or geometry changes such as after rotating can block motion, so check for blockage and replan. General principle: before any action, verify all preconditions—object location and proximity, held state, and path clearance—and use environment feedback. Sequence actions as navigate → pick → move → place, and avoid assuming manipulation or movement will succeed without verification.

## Preliminary Thinking
1) Identify the target object and the goal location. 2) Confirm the robot's current state, especially whether it is holding anything. 3) If the object is not held, locate it, navigate to it, verify it is within reach, and then pick it up. 4) Before placing, verify the robot is holding the object; if not, complete a pick action first. 5) Before moving, check the intended path for obstacles or blockages, especially after rotating, and replan if blocked. 6) Move to the goal location while monitoring feedback, then place the object. 7) After each action, check feedback; if a precondition failed or the action failed, diagnose the issue and replan rather than assuming success.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
